value.account:
Added pure scope auditing and projection-owned identity enumeration, strict loop progress validation, deterministic Workflow Lisp retry lineage, reached-call caller/alias/current-position checks and ordered predecessor audits. Integrated CLI and structural-root executor guards with authoritative checksum rechecks and atomic failure envelopes preserving forensic state. Projection diagnostics propagate unchanged through calls, routing, loops, finalization and session close; forensic cursors render pending and do not supply live heartbeat state. Added source-position-aware YAML import ambiguity rejection and compiler-owned Workflow Lisp provenance, preserving classic imported bundle identity. Updated specs/state.md, acceptance entries, behavioral tests, affected fixtures and only the newly required projection metadata in structural snapshots. State schema remains 2.1, with no new dependency or run-layout change.

Considered checksum-only guarding, name/suffix recovery, eager recursive validation and persisted audit records; rejected them because they respectively miss compatible identity drift, can choose the wrong owner, violate reached-call validation precedence, or introduce stale authority and unnecessary persistence. Reused the existing projection, lifecycle and atomic-write mechanisms instead. Verification: final targeted tests 115 passed; 124 tests collected across new/extended modules; loader/compiler/build checks 371 passed; related runtime checks 118 passed; CLI observability/materialized-view checks 34 passed; orchestrator dry-run smoke passed; git diff --check passed. Final full suite: 4,803 passed, 13 skipped, 46 failed. All 46 failing node IDs exactly match failures reproduced with HEAD Python source without changing the checkout. Those unrelated baseline failures were not repaired, and skipped external/provider coverage was not claimed. Previously tolerated stale or ambiguous durable identities now intentionally reject resume.
value.summary: Hardened checksum-compatible resume with exact projection ownership audits, deterministic retry lineage and sticky privacy-safe failures before effects.
